records.name: SideQuest Theater
records.summary: An improv theater near Rittenhouse Square that offers beginner workshops and improv classes and puts on its own shows, including a show running October 2 to 25, 2026.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner workshop or an improv class, or come see the theater's own shows.

schedule.text: Beginner workshops and improv classes are offered, but the site does not list class days or times. Camp Dread runs October 2 to 25, 2026.

cost.text: Class prices are not listed. Show tickets are sold through CrowdWork.

first_step.how: Use the contact email or join the mailing list to ask about the next beginner workshop
first_step.basis: The site lists beginner workshops and improv classes and gives a contact email and a mailing list.

records.notes: Class times and prices are not on the site. A summer camp is named in the menu with no details. The show run dates are the dated evidence.

records.name: Philly Improv Theater (PHIT)
records.summary: An improv and sketch comedy training group in Old City with beginner clinics, a longer intensive, and a community night that mixes a short improv show with an open jam.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner clinic or class, then join the open jam at a Community Night.

schedule.text: Community Night (a low-pressure improv show plus open jam) is next on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Improv Essentials, a 3-week beginner clinic, starts October 5. Improv 101 Intensive starts October 27. Class days and times are not listed.

cost.text: Class prices are not listed. Community Night has a $10 venue cover charged by the venue, not by the group.

first_step.how: Register for a beginner clinic such as Improv Essentials through the group's website
first_step.basis: Runs a 3-week beginner clinic and an open jam for people new to improv.

records.notes: Community Night is for people 21 and up with ID, and it is held at a venue that charges a cover. The site and its social feed give different venue details for Community Night and different dates for an info session, so those are not recorded. The founding history on the 2016 wiki page is old and not used for status.

records.name: Sawubona Creativity Project
records.summary: An arts space on East Passyunk Avenue that hosts a free monthly open mic for stand-up and storytelling, where performers sign up on the night.
records.what_you_do: Sign up at the door to perform a short set in the monthly open mic, or come to watch.

schedule.text: Hoodwink! stand-up and storytelling open mic on the third Sunday of each month, 7 to 8 pm, with sign-ups from 6:30 pm. The next date is October 18, 2026.

first_step.how: Arrive by 6:30 pm and sign up on the spot
first_step.basis: The open mic is free and open to anyone who signs up on the night.

records.notes: The group's own site lists no dated events and no regular jam schedule. The Creative Philadelphia listing is the dated evidence. The site describes the group as a sponsored project of Fractured Atlas, a nonprofit arts service organization. A search snippet mentioned a first-Sunday jam and LGBTQ and BIPOC nights, but I could not confirm it, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Jazz Attack
records.summary: A nonprofit swing dance group that runs a lesson and social dancing every Thursday night, with live jazz on some nights.
records.what_you_do: Take the beginner lesson, then dance socially until 11 pm. Volunteers get in free.

schedule.text: Every Thursday: lesson 8 to 9 pm (a beginner lesson is included with admission), then social dancing 9 to 11 pm. Live music is usually on the second Thursday of the month.

locations.label: Dance hall in the Philadelphia Boys Choir and Chorale building

cost.text: DJ nights $10 ($7 for students). Band nights $15 ($10 for students). Free for volunteers.

first_step.how: Arrive for the 8 pm lesson, which is included with admission
first_step.basis: A beginner lesson runs before social dancing every Thursday and is included in the ticket, so newcomers can drop in.

records.notes: The site has no email or phone, and says the quickest way to reach the group is Instagram messenger (handle @JazzAttackSwings, Facebook and Instagram). The newest dated item is a Winter Formal photo caption from January 2026. The copyright footer is not used as evidence.

records.name: Thursday Night Contra Dance (PATMAD)
records.summary: A weekly contra dance in Mount Airy run by the nonprofit Philadelphia Area Traditional Music and Dance group, with a beginner lesson before each dance.
records.what_you_do: Join the beginner lesson at 7:30 pm, then the dance from 8 to 10:30 pm.

schedule.text: Every Thursday: beginner lesson at 7:30 pm, dancing from 8 to 10:30 pm.

locations.label: The Irish Center (Commodore John Barry Arts and Cultural Center), ballroom entrance

cost.text: Pay what you wish, with a suggested $10, $15 or $20 or more.

first_step.how: Arrive by 7:30 pm for the beginner lesson before the dance starts at 8
first_step.basis: A beginner lesson starts every week before the dance and the price is pay what you wish, so newcomers can drop in.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a ContraCopia dance weekend announced for Friday November 27 to Sunday November 29, 2026, with registration open. The date the announcement was posted is not shown. An older welcome page lists the dance ending at 11 pm, but the current page says 10:30 pm, which is used. The page names a contact form but shows no email address.

records.name: Old Academy Players
records.summary: A community theater on Indian Queen Lane where every role is filled by an unpaid volunteer, and where crew help is needed for set and tech strike and build sessions.
records.what_you_do: Audition for a play, or sign up to help with the sets, tech or hospitality for a show.

schedule.text: Auditions: Venus in Fur on Saturday, November 7, 2026 at 10 am (sign-in closes 11:30 am). Bug on Saturday, November 21, 2026 at 10 am, with walk-in check-in until 12:30 pm and a weather backup on December 5. Crew strike and build sessions are set for Sunday, January 24, 2027 at 4:30 pm and Sunday, March 21, 2027 at 5 pm.

cost.text: The audition fee is not stated. All roles are unpaid volunteer roles.

first_step.how: Come to an audition (Venus in Fur on November 7, or Bug on November 21 with walk-ins), or ask the theater how to help with crew
first_step.basis: Public audition calls, with walk-in check-in for Bug, and volunteers are needed for crew work.

records.notes: The audition notices do not show when they were posted. The nonprofit wording came from the theater's audition page text in a search result, not from the page I fetched. The Venus in Fur director's personal address is on the page but left out. The page lists crew needs only under Venus in Fur, not Bug.

records.name: Philadelphia Suns Lion Dance
records.summary: A volunteer-run nonprofit in Chinatown with a lion dance troupe that teaches people of all ages on Sundays and performs at Lunar New Year and other events.
records.what_you_do: Learn lion dance drumming and moves at Sunday practice, or help look after the lion heads and costumes.

schedule.text: Sunday practice from 1 to 2:30 pm. The practice season starts the weekend after Labor Day and runs until Lunar New Year.

cost.text: Not stated on the group's site.

first_step.how: Email liondance@phillysuns.org or come to a Sunday practice
first_step.basis: The site says practice is open to anyone who wants to learn and that all ages and skill levels are welcome, and it gives an email address.

records.notes: The group's own page has only a 2022 copyright footer, which is not used as evidence. The February 2026 WHYY article is the dated evidence and calls the group a nonprofit that started in 1972 as a basketball club. The site's practice section links to liondance@phillysuns.com, but its contact section uses the .org address, so the .org address is used. The 2026 Lunar New Year workshop listing is an event, not recorded.

records.name: Penn Lions
records.summary: A University of Pennsylvania student lion dance troupe, founded in 2007, with close to 30 student members. It performs and hosts intercollegiate lion dance events.
records.what_you_do: Student members learn lion dance together and perform at campus and regional events.
records.notes: The newest dated item on the page is the 2024 hosting of an intercollegiate competition, given by year only. The page gives no recruitment timing, tryout rules, or practice times, so there is no first step. A search snippet said the troupe recruits each fall, which is not verified. The email on the page is listed for booking.

records.name: Troupe Da Da African Dance and Drum Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia African dance and drum ensemble formed in 1992 that performs and has brought African dance into schools.
records.what_you_do: Ask the ensemble about classes, rehearsals and performances, since the site does not publish a schedule.

schedule.text: No class or rehearsal schedule is published on the site.

first_step.how: Call, email, or use the contact page to ask how to take part

records.notes: The newest dated items on the site are from 2018 (a stilt walking show and school work), given by year only, so status is unknown rather than dormant. The Mann Center and ODUNDE Festival mentions are undated. Teaching details from a search snippet were not verified and are not recorded.

records.name: Patchwork: A Storytelling Guild
records.summary: A storytelling guild that puts on public story nights and showcases, with free or pay-what-you-can tickets, at venues that include The Rotunda on Walnut Street.
records.what_you_do: Come to a story night as an audience member, or apply to tell a story at a showcase. Story swaps need registration through the site's links.

schedule.text: Public story nights and showcases several times a year, mostly at The Rotunda on Walnut Street and at the Chestnut Hill Library, plus some at Charles A. Brown Ice House in Bethlehem. The next listed event is Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 7 pm at the Ice House. Most items are one-off events.

cost.text: Free or pay what you can. Some shows suggest $15.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a story night, or use the teller application or the open call linked from the site
first_step.basis: Public shows are open to anyone, and teller applications and story swap registration are separate steps the page describes.

records.notes: Many listed items have no year. Only items whose weekday matches 2026 were treated as current, and the October 24, 2026 Saturday event is the one used. Some older teller deadlines on the page are struck through and unclear. This is a set of events, not a weekly group.

records.name: Power Street Theatre
records.summary: A community arts and theater group that runs a monthly Sunday open mic with spoken word, music and comedy, and free adult courses in storytelling, theater and comedy.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the open mic to share a poem, story, song or joke, or join a free adult course, where the site says no experience is needed.

schedule.text: Souletri Sunday open mic, monthly on Sundays at 2 pm at Two Locals Brewing Co., with dates on October 25 and November 29, 2026. Latin Social Happy Hour dates are October 15, November 19 and December 15, 2026. Land and Body Student Showcase is November 21, venue to be announced.

cost.text: Land and Body courses, the open mic and the Latin Social events are free. Donations go to the group's programs.

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday open mic, or sign up for a Land and Body course
first_step.basis: The open mic is free and public, and the adult courses say no experience is needed, but the sign-up steps for courses were not on the page I read.

records.notes: The page gives event dates without a year. 2026 was chosen because the weekdays match that year. Nonprofit status is not stated on the page I read, although a search snippet calls it nonprofit, so the kind is left as program. The page does not say the Latin Social events are dance nights, so they are not tagged as social dance.

records.name: The Savoy Company
records.summary: A nonprofit Gilbert and Sullivan company that has put on operettas since 1901, run by volunteer members from the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the Join Savoy interest form, or meet members at a public performance.

schedule.text: Outdoor performance of Trial By Jury on Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 6 pm at Stoneleigh (gates at 5 pm, rain date August 16). Rehearsal and crew schedules are not on the page.

first_step.how: Submit the interest form at the Join Savoy page, or email the recruitment address
first_step.basis: Anyone can send an interest form, but the page posts no audition or volunteer crew dates.

records.notes: This group is based in Norristown and recruits from the wider Philadelphia area, so it is marked outside the city. Older listings show a Philadelphia P.O. box and a different address, so verify the current one. The recruitment email is joinsavoy@gmail.com on the page, but it is left out of the contacts. Backstage crew work and rehearsal nights came only from search snippets, not from the page, so the stage crew tag is not added.

records.name: Danse4Nia
records.summary: A Philadelphia dance organization founded in 2006 that runs a youth company for ages 10 to 18, a professional company, and a conservatory with fall and spring sessions.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the conservatory's fall or spring session, or audition for the youth company.

schedule.text: The conservatory runs fall and spring sessions in a mix of online and in-person classes. The youth company is for ages 10 to 18. The home page lists no class times.

locations.label: Danse4Nia (on the Philadelphia Circus School campus)

cost.text: Fees are not shown on the home page.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page to ask how to join the conservatory or audition for the youth company
first_step.basis: The youth company takes auditions, and the get-started steps on the home page are not spelled out.

records.notes: Address conflict: this site gives 6452 Greene Street, a Yelp listing gives 6139 to 43 Germantown Avenue, and a directory gives 143 W Walnut Lane. The site address is used. The home page has no dated items, and the copyright footer is not used as evidence. No adult or African dance class schedule was found. A 2024 article describes weekly classes in 2023, which is too old to count. The email is on the contact page but was not shown in the summary.

records.name: Circle Theatre
records.summary: A community theater in Grand Rapids, Michigan, that recruits volunteers.
records.notes: Found in a Philadelphia search by mistake. The page gives a Grand Rapids, Michigan address. It does not serve Philadelphia.

records.name: Theatre 29
records.summary: A community theater in Twentynine Palms, California, that recruits volunteers for crew and front of house work.
records.notes: Found in a Philadelphia search by mistake. The page gives a California address and a 760 phone number. It does not serve Philadelphia.

records.name: Pennsylvania Youth Theatre
records.summary: A youth theater in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, with a volunteer crew for costumes, props, sets and ushering.
records.notes: The page gives a Bethlehem address (Lehigh Valley), not Philadelphia. Not published.

records.name: Lion Dance Plus (Young Audiences NJ and Eastern PA)
records.summary: A paid lion dance assembly performance for schools, booked through an arts-in-education program office.
records.notes: A school assembly booked by fee, not a group people join. Office in Princeton, New Jersey, with a Pennsylvania office at CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia.

records.name: Mixteco Ballet Folklorico
records.notes: The site gives a Houston, Texas address (404 East Burress Street) and no Philadelphia classes. It does not serve Philadelphia.

records.name: Gund Kwok
records.notes: A lion and dragon dance troupe for women of Asian descent, with a children's program. The site gives a Boston, Massachusetts address and no Philadelphia classes.

records.name: Philadelphia Folklore Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that documents, presents and teaches folk and traditional arts in the Philadelphia area. Its website lists no classes or dated events right now.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, join the mailing list, or attend its exhibitions, films and concerts when they are announced.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list or volunteer through the website
first_step.basis: No classes or events are listed now, so the clear ways in are volunteering and the mailing list.

records.notes: Folk arts rather than dance, so it sits at the edge of this lane and may fit the heritage or music lanes better. The newest dated item on the site is a February 26, 2025 news post about an archive. The footer year (2024) is not evidence. Older classes and a 2021 screening on Wikipedia are not used. The phone number is from the site's phone link.

records.name: Philadelphia Argentine Tango School
records.notes: A paid tango school at 2030 Frankford Avenue that sells classes through registration links. Its site shows no milonga schedule, class times or prices. The weekly Palermo Fishtown Milonga with a beginner class came from a listing snippet and was not confirmed on the site. The only date on the site is an old copyright line, which is not evidence. Business, so not published. The owner may want to decide whether tango school socials count as community programs.

records.name: Dance Philadelphia Argentine Tango (Friday milonga)
records.notes: A paid tango teacher's weekly Friday milonga at 1315 Buttonwood St, with an intermediate class at 8:30 pm and a free beginner class included with admission. Admission is $12, or $6 for full-time students, though the listing's price field shows $10. The listing shows an October 9, 2026 date. The organizer's site is lesleymitchell.com, which was not fetched. A December 2023 milonga at the same venue is marked ended. Business-run, so not published. The owner may want to decide whether teacher-run socials count as community programs.

records.name: Damian and Sarah Tango (South Philly Milonga)
records.notes: A tango teaching pair's afternoon milonga on the second Saturday of each month at 1630 South 19th Street, with an all-level class at 1 pm, dancing 2 to 6 pm, and a listed price of $17. The listing shows an October 10, 2026 date. The organizer's site was not fetched. Business-run, so not published.

records.name: The Living Arts Dance Studios
records.notes: A dance studio in Northern Liberties with a West African dance class for ages 6 and up. Season 21 registration is open for fall 2026, with classes starting September 8. The site mentions a foundation and says financial aid will be announced, but describes no community program, and its for-profit status is not stated. Treated as a business for now. The owner may want to review it, since the foundation could count as a community program.

leads_only.name: Mt. Airy Contra Dance
leads_only.note: Named in a search result and on a Meetup page. Not read. Check whether it is separate from the Thursday PATMAD dance.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Scottish Country Dance
leads_only.note: Search snippet says a beginner class meets most Fridays at 7:45 pm at the Lutheran Church of the Holy Communion on Sansom Street. Not verified on the group's own page.

leads_only.name: Giddy Up Philly (line dancing)
leads_only.note: Magazine article fetched: Friday beginner lesson 7 to 8 pm and dancing 8 to 10 pm, free, at Voyeur in the Gayborhood (moved from Tavern on Camac). Article dated March 21, year not shown. No group website or street address found.

blocked.note: Free Library Coffee and Conversations open mic event page returned 403. Not read. A search snippet listed 2026 dates, which were not recorded.
Contra dance listing page returned 403. Not read. Host group unknown.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls used (hard cap), so coverage is thinner than the 20 to 40 target. 32 fetches, 2 blocked pages (CDSS contra listing and a Free Library event). Records: 24. Verdicts: publish 14, out_of_area 5, not_a_group 5, hide 0, duplicate 0. Publish: SideQuest Theater, Philly Improv Theater (PHIT), Sawubona Creativity Project, Jazz Attack, Thursday Night Contra (PATMAD), Old Academy Players, Philadelphia Suns, Penn Lions (low confidence, students only), Troupe Da Da (status unknown), Patchwork Storytelling Guild, Power Street Theatre, The Savoy Company (Norristown, outside the city), Danse4Nia (status unknown), Philadelphia Folklore Project (folk arts, edge of this lane). Not recorded: Adath Israel Israeli dancing (Merion, outside the city, page last updated 2022) and Stardust Ballroom (Bellmawr, New Jersey) were named in search results with no link captured; Urban Movement Arts (Callowhill studio) had no link captured. Studios named in listings and not fetched: Society Hill Dance Academy, Philly Dance Fitness, Gwendolyn Bye Dance Center, Crossroads Irish Dancers, Coyle School of Irish Dance (Flourtown), Philly Bhangra Club (Oaks), Michael's Cafe (Bensalem). Open gaps: adult folklorico with beginner classes in Philadelphia (none found), Irish ceili or set dance groups (only studios found), square dance (none found), social dance groups in Germantown, Kensington and West Philadelphia, and any dance events at the Irish Center (its website was not in my results). Tango and line dance are mostly studio-run or leads so far.
